explanation: A 45-45-90 triangle is the right triangle you get by cutting a square along its diagonal: the two acute angles are equal (45° each), so the two legs are equal too. Because the legs are equal, the Pythagorean theorem gives hypotenuse = √(leg² + leg²) = leg·√2, which is why the sides always sit in the ratio 1 : 1 : √2. Moving the leg slider rescales the whole triangle, and the readout shows the hypotenuse staying exactly leg·1.414 — the √2 factor never changes, only the size does.
bullets: Equal 45° angles force the two legs to be equal in length.
Hypotenuse = leg·√2 comes straight from a² + a² = c².
Sides keep the fixed ratio 1 : 1 : √2 at any size.
It is exactly half of a square split along its diagonal.
